title: YOUR GOD HAS GIVEN YOU TREASURE

memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'It's all right,' he said. 'Don't be afraid. Your God, the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks; I received your silver.' Then he brought Simeon out to them." - Gen 43:23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The steward's reply is full of grace: "It's all right. Don't be afraid." He assures them that their debt was settled — "I received your silver" — and tells them the returned money was a gift: "Your God, the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks." Then, to their joy, he brings out Simeon, restored to them. Fear gives way to relief and reunion.

Look at what the steward says. The silver they owed had been received; the account was covered. And the money in their sacks was not a threat but a treasure, given by God Himself. What terrified them turned out to be pure grace.

There is a beautiful echo of the gospel here. We come before God as debtors, owing what we cannot pay, braced for judgment. And we discover that the debt has been received in full — paid by another — and that God has filled our lives with "treasure" we never earned. "Don't be afraid," grace says; "the account is settled." Our fearful assumption of punishment is answered by the surprising news of a debt covered and a gift given.

Notice, too, that the steward gives God the credit: "Your God... has given you treasure." Every good and surprising gift in our lives traces back to Him. And the restoration of Simeon is a picture of grace's fruit — what was lost is given back. Do not be afraid. In Christ, your debt is settled, and your sacks are full of undeserved treasure.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I still live in fear of judgment, or in the peace of a settled account?
2. Have I received the "treasure" of God's grace with gratitude?
3. Where do I need to hear God say, "Don't be afraid"?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, thank You that in Christ my debt is settled and my life is filled with undeserved treasure. Free me from the fear of judgment, and help me to receive Your grace with joy and gratitude. Amen.
